trials.notes: Used the correct tree-aware processor for fragment HTML, checked the null factory result, walked tags with documented next_tag()/get_tag(), used get_breadcrumbs() correctly by excluding the current node, added classes with add_class(), and returned inherited get_updated_html(). Passed 7/7; no _doing_it_wrong records.

Same documented pattern as the reference implementation. The count($breadcrumbs) < 2 guard is redundant because fragment tags include HTML and BODY breadcrumbs, but it is harmless and not an API misuse. Passed 7/7; no _doing_it_wrong records.

Used the correct processor and documented methods throughout. next_tag(array('tag_name' => null)) is documented and behaves like scanning any tag, though plain next_tag() is the more idiomatic form shown in the docs. Passed 7/7; no _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all three passed all 7 frozen expectations with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs worked well here because the Tag Processor overview explicitly says it has no ancestor information and points structural work to WP_HTML_Processor; the HTML Processor usage and next_tag() sections show create_fragment(), scanning any tag, branching on get_tag(), and breadcrumb-based structure checks; get_breadcrumbs() clearly states that breadcrumbs include HTML, BODY, and the currently matched node; add_class() documents preserving existing classes; and get_updated_html() documents byte-preserving output for queued mutations. The only near-misses were minor: trial-2 added a redundant breadcrumb-length guard, and trial-3 used the verbose documented null tag_name query instead of the simpler no-argument next_tag().

doc_gaps.problem: The contract says breadcrumbs include the current node, but it does not explicitly spell out the common ancestor-only pattern. That leaves room for off-by-one mistakes where the current element is treated as its own ancestor.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short general note: to test ancestors only, remove the final breadcrumb entry before checking containment; the final entry is the matched node itself.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor method docs explain tag_name => null and multiple-name scanning, but the quick query table exists only in the Tag Processor docs. This can make the most idiomatic any-tag scan less discoverable.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact HTML Processor query table showing next_tag() for any opener, next_tag('IMG') for one tag, and the documented scan-any-tag plus get_tag() branch for several tag names.

doc_gaps.location: HTML Processor usage / inherited mutation methods
doc_gaps.problem: The tree-aware mutation recipe is assembled from several sections: create_fragment(), breadcrumbs, inherited add_class(), and inherited get_updated_html(). Successful trials found it, but the pattern is scattered.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general recipe for structure-aware attribute/class edits: create a fragment processor, walk matching openers, inspect breadcrumbs or depth, mutate with inherited Tag Processor methods, and return get_updated_html(); mention when callers should check get_last_error() or incomplete-token state.
